evals.name: session-with-card
evals.prompt: I shot the first batch of dishes for our tablet menu yesterday on my phone: 11 dish photos and 2 turntable clips are in <inputs>/session-with-card/raw (photos/ and video/). IMG_0001.jpg is the grey card frame I took first under the same light; IMG_0006 came out as HEIC for some reason. Please prepare the menu media for the tablets — the photos and the loops — and tell me which shots I should redo. Don't touch the originals; build the project in <outputs>/project.
evals.expected_output: A calibrated session from the card frame, graded sRGB JPEGs for every photo (HEIC included), two seamless SDR loops, contact sheets and frame grids used for QA, a QA report, a delivery folder, and a short list of shots to redo with reasons (hand, chopsticks, drink cans, phone watermark, duplicates).
expectations: Every one of the 11 dish photos (IMG_0002..IMG_0012, including the HEIC IMG_0006) has a graded output JPEG, or is excluded with a stated content reason (hand, clutter, not a dish)
Delivered photos are JPEG with an sRGB profile or no profile (never Display P3), long edge at most 2560 px, orientation baked in (no EXIF orientation other than 1)

White balance is derived from the card frame: relative to the raw files, the graded photos' R/G and B/G change by the gains that neutralise the card (within 0.06 / 0.08), and a graded card patch, if delivered uncropped, is neutral within 3/255
Each clip that shows the dish became an SDR H.264 loop (yuv420p, no audio, long edge at most 1920, faststart); a clip that does not show the dish is named as such and left out
Delivered loops are seamless: last-frame to first-frame similarity at least 0.95 (or no loop was delivered because the clip is not the dish, stated in the notes)
Delivered loops hold one revolution (moon 12.0 s ± 0.3 s, swift 10.0 s ± 0.3 s) or a stated ping-pong (or no loop was delivered because the clip is not the dish)
Contact sheets of the graded photos exist (a QA image at most 1568 px on the long edge with several thumbnails) and the notes say they were judged as sheets, not file by file
A QA report exists that names at least one flagged photo (clipping, exposure outlier, cast, matte) with a reason
The final answer names specific shots to redo with concrete reasons (hand, chopsticks or spoon in frame, drink cans, phone watermark, near-duplicate angles)
No original was modified: every file under the read-only input folder has the same checksum after the run

evals.name: no-card-mixed
evals.prompt: Our menu photos are a mess: a few from a photographer with a proper camera and some from my phone, all in <inputs>/no-card-mixed/raw/photos. We never shot a grey card. Make them look consistent for the tablets and cut the dishes out onto a cream background (#F6F4EF) with a soft shadow. Don't modify the originals; put the project in <outputs>/project.
evals.expected_output: An honest handling of the missing card (neutral reference from a white plate or a clearly stated assumption), one look applied to all, cutouts on #F6F4EF with a contact shadow and confidence flags, contact sheets, a report that names the interior shots (khmer_01, khmer_02) as not dish photos and the cross-session exposure/cast outliers, and a statement that photos from different lights cannot truly share one look.
expectations: Every one of the 7 photos has a graded output JPEG, or is explicitly excluded in the notes with a reason
Every delivered dish is a cutout on #F6F4EF (corners within ±4/255), or a graded photo whose matte failure is explained in the notes; at least one cutout exists
Each cutout carries a soft contact shadow rather than a hard paste: a band of pixels between 3 and 60 levels darker than the background covers at least 0.5% of the image
The missing grey card is handled explicitly: the notes state which neutral reference (white plate rim, assumption, auto) set white balance and exposure, and what that costs
khmer_01 and khmer_02 (dining-room interiors with no dish in frame) are identified as unsuitable for a dish menu and excluded or flagged
Cross-session differences are reported: exposure or cast outliers are listed, or the notes say photos from different cameras and lights cannot fully share one look
The delivered set is even: the median luminance (Y50) of the delivered photos spans at most 0.20
Contact sheets exist (a QA image at most 1568 px with several thumbnails) and were used to judge the batch
Matte quality is assessed per file: a confidence score or flag per cutout, or per-file matte notes naming the doubtful ones
No original was modified: every file under the read-only input folder has the same checksum after the run

evals.name: loops-and-hdr
evals.prompt: The photos were graded last week; the session file is <inputs>/loops-and-hdr/work/session.json. Now the four turntable clips in <inputs>/loops-and-hdr/raw/video need to become loops for the tablets with the same look as the photos. moon-hdr.mov looks grey and washed out on my laptop, and al92.mov I'm not sure even turns the right way. Originals are read-only; write to <outputs>/project.
evals.expected_output: Four H.264 SDR loops at 1080p with the session look baked in via a LUT: moon and swift cut to exactly one revolution (or ping-pong with a stated reason), moon-hdr tone-mapped to SDR first (not merely re-encoded), al92's ambiguous period detected and handled (ping-pong or an explicit duration chosen from the frame grid), frame grids with seam scores, and video QA stats.
expectations: Four loops exist (moon, swift, al92, moon-hdr) as H.264 MP4, yuv420p, no audio, long edge at most 1920
moon and swift loops are seamless: last-frame to first-frame similarity at least 0.95
moon-hdr was tone-mapped, not merely re-encoded: its loop is tagged bt709 (or untagged SDR) and its mean luminance is within 10% of the moon loop's
The session look was applied to the clips: relative to the source frame, the loop's B/G rises and R/G falls in the direction of the session's white-balance gains
al92's ambiguous rotation is handled: the notes mention the ambiguous or symmetric period (or a checked frame grid) and state the chosen loop mode or duration
Frame grids or equivalent QA images (at most 1568 px) exist for every loop
Seam or loop-quality scores are recorded for at least three clips (video_stats.json or the notes)
No original was modified: every file under the read-only input folder has the same checksum after the run

evals.name: pattaya-menu
evals.prompt: Our photographer shot 15 dishes for the tablet menu at the restaurant, they're in <inputs>/pattaya-menu/raw/photos. No grey card, same place but not all on the same evening. Make them look consistent for the tablets, keep the whole plate in the frame, and no background removal, we want the table showing. Originals are read-only; build the project in <outputs>/project.
evals.expected_output: Per-file white balance and exposure from a plate patch in each photo (no card), one shared look, crops that keep the whole plate with a margin (or a stated reason when the source already cut it), no cutouts, contact-sheet QA, a QA report and a delivery folder with 15 photos, plus reshoot advice for the two plates the photographer cut.
expectations: Every one of the 15 photos has a graded output JPEG, or is excluded with a stated content reason
Delivered photos are JPEG with an sRGB profile or no profile, long edge at most 2560 px, orientation baked in
The plates read neutral after correction: in at least 12 of the delivered photos the bright low-chroma pixels (the plate) are within 6/255 of neutral
The batch is even: the plate brightness (95th-percentile luminance) of the delivered photos spans at most 0.15
The vessel is whole: no delivered photo cuts the plate (rembg matte touching the frame edge on more than 1% of the border) unless the source photo already did
The delivered photos keep their real background: no cutout on a plain colour was delivered
Contact sheets exist (a QA image at most 1568 px with several thumbnails) and the notes say they were judged as sheets
A QA report exists that names at least one flagged photo with a reason
The final answer names the plates the photographer cut (club sandwich, steak with mash) as reshoot candidates or explains the crop choice for them
No original was modified: every file under the read-only input folder has the same checksum after the run

evals.name: loops-real
evals.prompt: Here are the turntable clips for the menu, in <inputs>/loops-real/raw/video, and the session file from the photo grading at <inputs>/loops-real/work/session.json. Some of the dishes only turn part of the way in the clip, one is upright/portrait, and raspberries-hdr.mov looks flat and grey on my laptop. Make them all loop for the tablets with the photo look. Originals are read-only; write to <outputs>/project.
evals.expected_output: SDR H.264 loops at 1080p for every dish clip: partial rotations as ping-pong (a revolution cut would jump), full turns as revolutions, the portrait clip kept upright, the HDR clip tone-mapped before grading, the clip with a person excluded with a reason, direction per clip with the one that turns the other way flagged, frame grids and seam scores, QA report.
expectations: Every clip that shows a dish without a person became an SDR H.264 loop (yuv420p, no audio, long edge at most 1920); cake_with_baker is excluded or flagged with a reason (person in frame)
Delivered loops are seamless: last-frame to first-frame similarity at least 0.95 for each
Partial rotations (raspberries, tomato_juice, baked_dish, chocolate_cake) are exported as ping-pong (or a stated dissolve), not cut as a fake revolution
The HLG clip was tone-mapped before grading: raspberries-hdr's loop is SDR (bt709 or untagged, yuv420p) with mean luminance within 10% of the raspberries loop
The portrait clip stays upright: the chocolate_cake loop is taller than wide with a long edge at most 1920
Turning direction is recorded for at least four clips and the clip that turns the other way (cake_stand, counter-clockwise) is flagged direction_mismatch or named in the notes
Frame grids (at most 1568 px) exist for every delivered loop
The session look was applied to the clips: relative to the source frame, a loop's B/G rises and R/G falls in the direction of the session gains
No original was modified: every file under the read-only input folder has the same checksum after the run
